truth_states: FACT = source-derived; UPSTREAM = in-tree doc claim; INFERENCE = labeled reasoning; AUTHORITY = HX governance decision

entries.name: nextjs-app-router-file-system-route-registration
entries.purpose: All API endpoints are registered by Next.js App Router file-system convention (688 route.ts files measured under src/app/api/, 102 top-level domain dirs), with static/dynamic segments taking precedence over catch-alls and rewrites defined in next.config.mjs; no global middleware.ts exists (ls-verified absent at src/middleware.ts, src/app/middleware.ts, middleware.ts), so interception is route-specific. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — registration is implicit in file layout, so an accidentally added route.ts is automatically exposed without a registration review gate
entries.test_contract: Direct: probe representative routes per domain; negative: confirm no global middleware interception by observing per-route CORS/auth behavior; inventory: re-count route.ts files and diff against this ledger's 688
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove or rename the route.ts file; Next.js stops serving the path (no central registry to revert)

entries.name: openai-compatible-v1-core-traffic-surface
entries.purpose: The /api/v1 tree (98 route.ts files measured, 45 subdomains: chat, completions, models, embeddings, responses, images, audio, batches, files, moderations, rerank, messages, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, videos, etc.) exposes the OpenAI-compatible client traffic surface. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — this is the primary model-traffic entry surface; misbehavior here misroutes or exposes all downstream model traffic
entries.test_contract: Direct HTTP against representative endpoints (/v1/models GET, /v1/chat/completions POST) asserting OpenAI-shaped JSON; negative: unknown /v1/* path returns JSON 404 not HTML
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove route files under src/app/api/v1/; paths fall through to the /v1 catch-all JSON 404

entries.name: v1-chat-completions-main-chat-entry
entries.purpose: POST /v1/chat/completions validates a deliberately permissive Zod-lite body shape, runs admission control and the prompt-injection guard, then delegates to handleChat in src/sse/handlers/chat.ts with single-parse body threading and early-stream keepalive. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — hottest path in the proxy; every chat request passes through this handler's admission, guard, and delegation logic
entries.test_contract: Direct: POST minimal valid body and assert SSE/JSON response shape; negative: malformed body rejected without stack leakage; routed: combo model name resolves through combo engine
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/route.ts; endpoint returns the /v1 catch-all JSON 404

entries.name: v1-root-models-listing
entries.purpose: GET /v1 (and OPTIONS preflight) delegates to the same unified models catalog builder as /api/v1/models, returning the OpenAI-compatible model list. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — read-only catalog projection with no mutation path
entries.test_contract: Direct: GET /v1 returns JSON model list consistent with /v1/models; OPTIONS returns CORS headers
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove src/app/api/v1/route.ts; /v1 root falls to the catch-all JSON 404

entries.name: v1beta-gemini-shaped-models-surface
entries.purpose: The /api/v1beta/models tree (plus a [...path] catch-all) serves the Gemini-shaped models API surface, built from PROVIDER_MODELS and synced/custom model stores. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — a second protocol surface duplicating model exposure; drift between it and /v1 can leak inconsistent model availability
entries.test_contract: Direct: GET /v1beta/models returns Gemini-shaped list; routed: /v1beta/models/<model>:generateContent path resolves via [...path] route
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove src/app/api/v1beta route files; surface 404s

entries.name: api-and-v1-json-404-catch-alls
entries.purpose: Catch-all routes under /api/* (issue #6424) and /v1/* (issue #6405) return structured JSON 404 (error.type not_found, code unknown_route) instead of the dashboard HTML shell, keeping unknown-route failures distinguishable from auth-scope failures. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — if these catch-alls shadowed a real route (they must not, per App Router precedence), endpoints would silently 404; their correctness is a negative-space guarantee
entries.test_contract: Negative: GET/POST unknown paths under /api/ and /v1/ return JSON 404 with code unknown_route and no HTML; regression: real routes still resolve (precedence)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the two catch-all route.ts files; unknown paths revert to Next.js not-found.tsx HTML

entries.name: management-plane-api-domains
entries.purpose: Roughly 100 top-level management domains under /api/ (combos, providers, keys, settings, quota, resilience, analytics, cli-tools, services, etc.) follow the pattern of gating each handler behind requireManagementAuth before any DB or mutation work, e.g. combos GET/POST. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — these domains mutate routing, credential, and policy state; an auth-gap in any one of ~100 domains is a full management-plane compromise
entries.test_contract: Auth-negative: unauthenticated request to each management domain returns 401/403; direct: authenticated CRUD round-trip on /api/combos; persistence: created combo survives restart
entries.rollback_or_disable: Per-route removal of route.ts; auth itself is fail-closed (handler returns early on authError)

entries.name: public-vs-management-route-classification-constants
entries.purpose: PUBLIC_API_ROUTE_PREFIXES (genuine subtrees, must end in /) and PUBLIC_API_ROUTES_EXACT (single paths) classify which API paths bypass dashboard auth, a shape-based split introduced for GHSA-74g9-q8f6-793h after a prefix-shadowing auth bypass. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: critical — a wrong entry in these lists silently reclassifies a management route as public, bypassing dashboard auth (the exact GHSA pattern the file documents)
entries.test_contract: Negative: every non-listed management path requires auth; unit: prefix entries all end in '/' and exact set matches only exact paths; regression: GHSA-74g9-q8f6-793h shadowing case
entries.rollback_or_disable: Revert the constants file; classification returns to the prior reviewed state

entries.name: combo-routing-engine-core
entries.purpose: handleComboChat (combo.ts) is the multi-model routing entry that expands combo configs via resolveComboTargets into ordered ResolvedComboTarget lists, then dispatches per-target through handleSingleModel with per-target error handling and circuit-breaker checks. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — the engine decides which provider/model/account serves every combo-routed request; a bug is systemic wrong-model routing (SEV-2 class)
entries.test_contract: Routed: request naming a combo resolves targets in strategy order; negative: all-targets-fail returns sanitized error; resilience: failing target falls through to next in order
entries.rollback_or_disable: Clients address concrete provider/model instead of combo names; combos are data, not code — no code rollback needed to stop using the engine

entries.name: strategy-dispatch-registry-gate
entries.purpose: HANDLED_COMBO_STRATEGIES is the runtime-explicit enumeration of the 20 strategies with real dispatch implementations (19 public + quota-share), kept equal to the canonical set by the G1 known-symbols gate in both directions. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — a verification/gate artifact; divergence fails a check rather than misrouting traffic
entries.test_contract: Unit: HANDLED_COMBO_STRATEGIES set equals ROUTING_STRATEGY_VALUES ∪ INTERNAL_ROUTING_STRATEGY_VALUES (canonicalSemDespacho / despachoNaoCanonico both empty)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove entries alongside their dispatch branches; the gate flags any mismatch

entries.name: account-fallback-strategy-values
entries.purpose: ACCOUNT_FALLBACK_STRATEGY_VALUES declares the 9 account-level fallback orderings (priority, weighted, fill-first, round-robin, p2c, random, least-used, cost-optimized, strict-random) consumed by validation schemas for per-connection fallback config. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — a constants enum; behavior lives in the account fallback service (adjacent partition)
entries.test_contract: Unit: schema accepts exactly the 9 declared values and rejects others; routed: per-connection fallback ordering follows the configured value
entries.rollback_or_disable: Static constant; revert edit to change the accepted set

entries.name: auto-routing-strategy-values
entries.purpose: AUTO_ROUTING_STRATEGY_VALUES declares 8 auto-router strategy names (rules, cost, eco, latency, fast, sla-aware, sla, lkgp) exposed to MCP tool schemas for auto-routing configuration. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — enum surface; note 8 names map onto 5 implementation classes via aliases (see CAP-P1-127), a naming drift to track
entries.test_contract: Unit: enum has exactly the 8 declared values; integration: each value resolves to a registered RouterStrategy (directly or via alias)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Static constant; revert edit

entries.name: openapi-spec-and-try-it-endpoints
entries.purpose: GET /api/openapi/spec returns the parsed openapi.yaml as a structured JSON catalog, and POST /api/openapi/try forwards a request to a local endpoint and returns the result (a docs 'Try It' proxy). [FACT — header comments; auth gating of try/route.ts not verified in this pass]
entries.risk_class: medium — the try-it proxy is an SSRF-shaped forwarding surface even if restricted to local endpoints
entries.test_contract: Direct: spec endpoint returns parsed catalog; negative: try-it rejects non-local or unauthenticated targets (auth behavior must be confirmed before any Layer-N exposure)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the two route files; docs lose spec/try features only

entries.name: routing-decision-explainability-endpoint
entries.purpose: GET /api/routing/decisions/<requestId> returns the recorded explanation of why a request was routed as it was, behind requireManagementAuth, via src/lib/usage/routeExplain. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — read-only explainability projection of routing logs
entries.test_contract: Direct: issue a routed request then fetch its decision record by requestId; auth-negative: unauthenticated fetch rejected
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the route file; explainability UI degrades, routing unaffected

entries.name: combo-adjacent-routing-helper-services
entries.purpose: Wildcard pattern matching for combo targets (wildcardMatch), task-type-based routing configuration (setTaskRoutingConfig), and prompt-intent classification (classifyPromptIntent) feed routing decisions outside the core strategy branches. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — these helpers influence target selection; misclassification silently changes which models serve traffic
entries.test_contract: Unit: wildcard specificity ordering; task-type mapping table; intent classification fixtures; routed: auto strategy consumes classifier output
entries.rollback_or_disable: Helpers are call-site gated; removing the call sites or config returns to static strategy behavior

entries.name: intelligent-adaptive-tag-reasoning-routing-modules
entries.purpose: A second tier of routing logic exists beside the combo engine: intelligent-vs-deterministic strategy categorization, tag-based routing normalization, adaptive candidate scoring/ranking, and reasoning-intent routing policy. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — overlapping routing authorities can produce non-obvious selection outcomes that are hard to attribute without the decision log
entries.test_contract: Unit per module (tag normalization, candidate scoring, reasoning intent extraction); routed: end-to-end selection matches the decision explanation record
entries.rollback_or_disable: Modules are opt-in via config; unsetting the corresponding routing config restores deterministic combo strategies

entries.name: routing-strategy-values-constants-registry
entries.purpose: ROUTING_STRATEGY_VALUES declares the canonical 19 public combo routing strategies and INTERNAL_ROUTING_STRATEGY_VALUES the 1 internal one (quota-share, deliberately never UI/API-selectable), with normalizeRoutingStrategy aliasing common synonyms and falling back to 'priority'. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — static constant registry with no runtime state; unknown values normalize to priority
entries.test_contract: Unit: array contains exactly 19 distinct public values plus 1 internal; normalizeRoutingStrategy maps 'usage'->least-used, 'context'->context-optimized, 'weekly-reset'/'reset-window-order'->reset-window, unknown->'priority'
entries.rollback_or_disable: Static constant; revert edit to change the set

entries.name: strategy-lkgp-last-known-good-provider
entries.purpose: The lkgp branch fetches the Last Known Good Provider record from localDb and moves the matching target (by provider+connectionId, with a defensive modelStr guard) to the front of the order. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — depends on persisted LKGP state; a stale record pins traffic to a degraded provider
entries.test_contract: Unit: matching target moves to index 0, already-first is a no-op, malformed modelStr does not crash; persistence: LKGP record survives restart and is honored
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo; failure to read LKGP is non-fatal (warns and keeps input order)

entries.name: strategy-strict-random
entries.purpose: The strict-random branch draws one target from a persistent per-combo deck (getNextFromDeck) and Fisher-Yates-shuffles the remainder so fallback load spreads instead of always hitting the top-priority model (issue #3959). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — selection is random but bounded by deck state; failure mode is uneven distribution, not wrong-model class
entries.test_contract: Unit: deck draw is deterministic per deck state and covers all targets over a full deck; remainder order varies across draws
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo; deck state is inert when unused

entries.name: strategy-random
entries.purpose: The random branch fully shuffles the ordered target list with Fisher-Yates for each request. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — pure permutation; no state
entries.test_contract: Unit: output is a permutation of input and order varies across calls
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo

entries.name: strategy-fill-first
entries.purpose: The fill-first branch deliberately preserves the incoming priority order unchanged (log-only no-op), filling the first target to its limits before falling through. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — identity transform on target order
entries.test_contract: Unit: output list identical to input list
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo

entries.name: strategy-p2c-power-of-two-choices
entries.purpose: The p2c branch reorders targets via orderTargetsByPowerOfTwoChoices, picking the better of two random candidates on load metrics to balance traffic. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — depends on the accuracy of per-target load metrics; bad metrics skew selection
entries.test_contract: Unit: with two candidates of known load, the less-loaded wins; distribution converges to balanced over many draws
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo

entries.name: strategy-least-used
entries.purpose: The least-used branch sorts targets by accumulated usage so the target with the fewest requests goes first. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — ordering by usage counters; counter corruption causes skew, not outage
entries.test_contract: Unit: target with lowest request count lands at index 0; counters increment after dispatch
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo

entries.name: strategy-cost-optimized
entries.purpose: The cost-optimized branch sorts targets cheapest-first and, when config.manifestRouting is true, applies manifest routing hints that can filter targets down to premium-eligible ones. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — pricing-table drift inverts the intended savings; manifest-filter errors fall back to standard ordering
entries.test_contract: Unit: targets sorted by ascending cost; with manifestRouting and a require-premium hint, ineligible targets are filtered; hint failure keeps cost order
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo or set manifestRouting false

entries.name: strategy-reset-aware
entries.purpose: The reset-aware branch orders targets by remaining quota relative to provider reset times via orderTargetsByResetAwareQuota. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — depends on fresh quota/reset data; stale quota snapshots misorder targets
entries.test_contract: Unit: target with most remaining quota first; negative: missing quota data degrades gracefully to input order
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo

entries.name: strategy-reset-window
entries.purpose: The reset-window branch orders targets by proximity to quota reset via orderTargetsByResetWindow (aliases weekly-reset / reset-window-order normalize here). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — same stale-quota-data dependency as reset-aware
entries.test_contract: Unit: target nearest its reset window is prioritized; alias strings normalize to reset-window
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo

entries.name: strategy-context-optimized
entries.purpose: The context-optimized branch sorts targets by context-window size, largest first, via sortTargetsByContextSize. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — static model metadata ordering; wrong metadata wastes context headroom, not correctness
entries.test_contract: Unit: largest-context target at index 0; ties stable
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo

entries.name: strategy-cache-optimized
entries.purpose: The cache-optimized branch expands and reorders targets by prompt-cache affinity (resolvePromptCacheAffinityKey / expandPromptCacheAffinityTargets / applyPromptCacheAffinity) so requests land on the provider holding their warm cache. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — affinity state can concentrate load on one target and starve fallback spread
entries.test_contract: Unit: repeat requests with the same affinity key resolve to the same target; affinity miss expands candidates
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo

entries.name: strategy-headroom
entries.purpose: The headroom branch orders targets by free capacity (most headroom first) via orderTargetsByHeadroom. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — depends on capacity/headroom telemetry accuracy
entries.test_contract: Unit: target with most free capacity at index 0; exhausted targets deprioritized
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo

entries.name: strategy-quota-share-internal
entries.purpose: The internal quota-share branch delegates to selectQuotaShareTarget (DRR + P2C in-flight + per-model bucket gating + per-connection concurrency caps) for system-minted qtSd/ quota-share combos, returning an idempotent in-flight slot release the caller must invoke (issue #11371). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — a leaked slot release degenerates selection into fewest-lifetime-dispatches and silently skews all quota-share traffic
entries.test_contract: Unit: selection respects DRR+P2C and concurrency caps; the returned release decrements in-flight exactly once; negative: strategy is absent from public ROUTING_STRATEGY_VALUES
entries.rollback_or_disable: Not user-selectable (kept out of ROUTING_STRATEGY_VALUES); removing the system combos that use it disables the path

entries.name: strategy-priority-default-order
entries.purpose: Priority is the default strategy (unknown values normalize to it): targets run in configured order, with a fallbackOnlyOnQuotaExhaustion gate that holds a priority target unless failure is quota-exhaustion or an open circuit breaker. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — the fallback gate can pin traffic on a failing primary for non-quota errors; that is intended but must be understood
entries.test_contract: Routed: targets attempted in configured order; with fallbackOnlyOnQuotaExhaustion, 4xx does not advance but quota exhaustion / OPEN breaker does
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo; the gate is config-driven per target

entries.name: strategy-weighted
entries.purpose: The weighted strategy picks targets by configured weights and supports sticky weighting (stickyWeightedLimit): a recent winner is re-prioritized across turns until the limit or eligibility change, at which point runtime units execute as priority. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — sticky state concentrates traffic; a stuck key pins one target until eviction
entries.test_contract: Unit: selection frequency converges to configured weights; sticky: same target reused up to the limit then released; negative: weightless targets never selected
entries.rollback_or_disable: Set stickyWeightedLimit to 1 (disables stickiness) or select another strategy

entries.name: strategy-round-robin
entries.purpose: Round-robin routes to a dedicated handleRoundRobinCombo path (unless a native Codex turn pin forbids rotation) and rotates runtime units from a sticky start index advanced per combo via rrCounters. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — rotation state is per-combo in-memory; a lost counter merely restarts the rotation
entries.test_contract: Unit: successive requests advance the start index modulo target count; native Codex pinned turns bypass rotation
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select another strategy on the combo; counters are inert when unused

entries.name: strategy-context-relay
entries.purpose: Context-relay resolves a relay config at setup and, after a successful turn on a handoff-listed provider (currently codex), fetches Codex quota windows for the session's connection to decide whether a context handoff should be generated; chat.ts injects the handoff after the real connectionId resolves. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — session-scoped handoff logic can move a conversation between accounts; mis-scope leaks context across connections
entries.test_contract: Routed: handoff only for handoffProviders-listed provider with resolvable session connectionId; negative: non-listed provider never triggers handoff
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove providers from relayConfig.handoffProviders or select another strategy

entries.name: strategy-auto
entries.purpose: The auto strategy resolves target ordering through tool-calling and context-window pre-filters, intent classification, quota-cutoff candidate building, explicit-router vs rules selection, and complexity-aware scoring with final dedup. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — it is the most autonomous selection path; scoring-weight or classifier drift changes model selection for every auto-routed request
entries.test_contract: Routed: tool-calling requests filter to tool-capable targets (fail-open only when compatFilterFailOpen); scoring order matches decision explanation; negative: empty candidate pool returns unavailableResponse
entries.rollback_or_disable: Select a static strategy on the combo; auto/* prefixes resolve to the same engine and can be unused without code change

entries.name: strategy-fusion
entries.purpose: Fusion fans the prompt out to a panel of models in parallel (minPanel quorum, 8s straggler grace, 90s hard cap, maxPanel 40 against heap OOM per issue #1905) and a configurable judge model synthesizes one answer from anonymized sources, degrading to a direct answer on a single survivor and 503 on total failure. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — multiplies upstream cost per request by panel size plus judge, and buffers full panel responses in memory (OOM history)
entries.required_authorization: owner — HX charter places fusion in the disabled-by-default agent-like class; enabling requires an owner decision [AUTHORITY]
entries.test_contract: Routed: panel fan-out returns one synthesized answer; negative: total panel failure returns 503, single survivor returns direct answer; load: panel size >40 rejected with 400
entries.rollback_or_disable: Do not configure fusion combos (strategy is opt-in per combo); per HX policy it stays disabled pending owner approval

entries.name: strategy-pipeline
entries.purpose: Pipeline runs combo targets in order as a sequential chain: each step's output becomes the next step's input with an optional per-step prompt injected as a system turn, intermediate steps forced non-streaming with tools stripped, and only the final step's response returned; transient step failures retry per combo retry config, non-transient fail immediately. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — chained model calls multiply latency/cost and a mid-chain failure discards all upstream work; per-step prompt injection is a prompt-composition surface
entries.required_authorization: owner — HX charter places pipelines in the disabled-by-default agent-like class; enabling requires an owner decision [AUTHORITY]
entries.test_contract: Routed: two-step chain threads step-1 output into step-2 and returns only the final answer; negative: transient 429/5xx intermediate retried, 4xx fails immediately without retry
entries.rollback_or_disable: Do not configure pipeline combos (strategy is opt-in per combo); per HX policy it stays disabled pending owner approval

entries.name: auto-combo-router-strategy-registry
entries.purpose: The auto-combo engine exposes 5 pluggable RouterStrategy classes (RulesStrategyImpl, CostStrategyImpl, LatencyStrategyImpl, SLAStrategyImpl, LKGPStrategyImpl) behind a name registry with aliases (eco->cost, fast->latency) and getStrategy fallback to 'rules' — so the 8 AUTO_ROUTING_STRATEGY_VALUES names map onto 5 implementations. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — registry with a safe default; the 8-names-to-5-classes aliasing is documentation drift risk, not a traffic risk
entries.test_contract: Unit: each of the 8 enum names resolves through getStrategy to a registered implementation; unknown name warns and falls back to rules
entries.rollback_or_disable: Config-driven (config.routerStrategy); unset restores default rules strategy

entries.name: packages-tree-routing-modules
entries.purpose: Searched packages/**/rout* per the partition source hint: the packages/ tree contains only browser-pool (and @omniroute/ holds opencode-plugin/opencode-provider); no routing modules exist under packages/. [FACT — searched, not found]
entries.risk_class: low — absence note; nothing to assess
entries.test_contract: Re-run find packages -iname '*rout*' on any future snapshot to confirm continued absence
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a

entries.name: express-fastify-koa-style-router-registration
entries.purpose: Searched src/, open-sse/, packages/ for express(), new Router(), and fastify( registration patterns: none found; all HTTP routing is Next.js App Router file-system convention. [FACT — searched, not found]
entries.risk_class: low — absence note
entries.test_contract: Re-grep registration patterns on any future snapshot
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a

entries.name: global-nextjs-middleware-interception
entries.purpose: Searched for a global Next.js middleware (src/middleware.ts, src/app/middleware.ts, middleware.ts): none exists, so CORS/auth/validation interception is implemented per-route, matching the upstream doc claim now verified against the tree. [FACT — searched, not found]
entries.risk_class: medium — without a global guard, every new route must remember its own auth/CORS; the publicApiRoutes classification (CAP-P1-008) is the compensating control
entries.test_contract: Re-check the three middleware paths on any future snapshot; spot-check new routes for the CORS/auth pattern
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a

entries.name: central-route-registry-or-manifest-module
entries.purpose: Searched for a central route registry/manifest module (*routeRegistry*, *routeManifest*, routes.ts): none found; registration is purely file-system convention, and the nearest artifact is the auth-classification constant list (src/shared/constants/publicApiRoutes.ts) which classifies but does not register routes. [FACT — searched, not found]
entries.risk_class: low — absence note; inventory must be derived by tree walks (as this ledger does), not by reading a registry
entries.test_contract: Re-run the registry filename search on any future snapshot
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a
